answer: Temporal diversity at the nebula: each identity's submission window is drawn from a random schedule, so one operator must sustain presence across thousands of staggered slots. Juniper scoring weights distinct-window streaks, forcing attackers to burn 500+ CPU-hours per identity to fake continuity. A ripple of missed windows slashes rewards below the ~$12/identity cost, so farming 100 sybils loses money before the 20th. It works because randomized timing converts cheap parallelism into expensive, unshareable waiting.
